authority.source: Owner decision 2026-10-19: a bounded checked claim and an unbounded kernel-checked obligation; every definition is recovered from the withdrawal-queue contract.

scope: Accepted keeper ticks of the withdrawal-queue vault, observed through the checked contract adapter.

trace.event_schema: withdrawal-queue tick/1: pre-vault after the decisions since the previous tick, alarm, payout and post-vault
trace.order: authoritative commit order of the accepted keeper ticks
trace.projection: one event per accepted keeper tick; deposits, requests and rejections between two ticks are hidden and reach the next tick only through its pre-vault
trace.model: the generated withdrawal-queue V2 contract evaluated by its checked Authority over every vault reachable from its genesis and the complete declared command and context domain
trace.environment: any commands from any caller between two ticks, and either alarm value at each tick; the alarm is taken as given
trace.initialization: the contract genesis commits, a changed genesis is refused, and no request is pending at genesis, so a history before its first tick holds no presented request
trace.transitions: every event is a keeper tick decided by the checked Authority on a vault reachable from the genesis
trace.continuity: hidden decisions leave the controller part unchanged except that an accepted request turns its own empty lane arrived; every tick leaves no lane arrived, so each accepted request is presented by exactly one tick

assumptions.definition: Unconditional requirement over recorded keeper ticks; provided true.

R.definition: the tick presents lane r's request: the lane is arrived before the tick because its owner's request was accepted after the previous tick (rule 6 presents every arrived lane, so each accepted request is presented exactly once).

C.definition: the decision is a keeper tick that pays lane r (rule 6, law 501): it queues one settlement payout of lane r with the amount that lane's request recorded, and empties the lane.

Tick.clause: the event is a keeper tick
Tick.definition: the event is an accepted keeper tick; every event of this projection is one, so it only requires that recorded events exist.

definitions.name: Ahead
definitions.clause: at least seven further keeper ticks are recorded

readings.body: forall sigma in Traces: forall r in Requests: always((R(r) and Ahead()) => within(7, C(r)))
readings.intuitive: every withdrawal request is paid by the eighth keeper tick that sees it, counting the tick that first presents it, whenever those ticks are recorded
readings.plain: once seven further keeper ticks have followed the tick that presents a withdrawal, it has been paid, alarms included

fixtures.note: Contract tick history: both lanes are presented under a sustained alarm; lane A is paid at the fourth tick and lane B at the eighth, exactly at the bound.
Contract tick history: the alarm defers lane A at the last recorded tick. Its window is not recorded, so the finite target asks nothing of it; the unbounded obligation keeps it.
Contract tick history: vacuous without a request; the pilot separately requires presented requests under active alarms.
Not a contract history (the pilot checks that the contract excludes it): lane A stays unpaid for eight recorded ticks.

formula: forall sigma in Traces: forall r in Requests: always((R(r) and Ahead()) => within(7, C(r)))
